sections.content: You know *porque* and *por eso* from A2 Unit 5 and *debido a* from B1 Unit 11. New here: *ya que* gives a reason like *porque*, and *como consecuencia* introduces a result. Together they link an environmental problem with its cause and its effect.

items.spanish: Hay menos agua porque ha habido una sequía.
items.english: There is less water because there has been a drought.

items.spanish: La contaminación ha aumentado; por eso, debemos actuar.
items.english: Pollution has increased; therefore, we must act.

items.spanish: Debido a la sequía, el nivel del río ha bajado.
items.english: Due to the drought, the river level has fallen.

items.spanish: Como consecuencia, algunas especies han desaparecido.
items.english: As a consequence, some species have disappeared.

sections.content: *Ya que* opens a sentence naturally: *Ya que ha habido una sequía, hay menos agua.* *Porque* more often follows the result: *Hay menos agua porque ha habido una sequía.*
